correctness.rationale: The RK stage chain telescopes to the exact Taylor polynomial on the planar oscillator; stage derivatives span the plane. The predictor never vanishes for degrees one through five. A verified polynomial identity yields the phase-speed numerator for each m. Degrees one through four have positive phase speed and total finite angle variation less than \(2\pi\). For degree five, the quartic \(F(x)=x^4-16x^3+2880\) has exactly two positive roots by derivative signs and exact brackets \((6,7)\) and \((15,16)\); the corresponding phase extrema lie on opposing sides of \(\pi/2\). This proves the exact three-preimage window. Standalone 754-check algebraic/rational/numerical tests verified ancillary computation and stage implementation but are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a sharp structural boundary for energy-preserving numerical time integration: an exactly norm-preserving projected RK step has three distinct positive time steps corresponding to one identical numerical rotation, while all smaller Taylor degrees lack this effect. The full inverse-image classification quantifies phase nonidentifiability, a material failure mode for phase-based step adaptation and oscillator timing even where invariant drift is exactly zero.
